strengths: Comprehensive empirical study systematically characterizing activation sparsity across multiple model families, sizes, and training methods with clear practical relevance
Simple, universal top-p framework that is parameter-free, requires no auxiliary training, and enables fair comparison across models and modules
Thorough experimental evaluation covering Gemma3, LLaMA3, Qwen2.5 with extensive task evaluation and first analysis of diffusion LLMs
Clear, actionable findings including the surprising result that input sparsity matches/exceeds gate sparsity, and evidence that data-free methods outperform calibration-based approaches
Excellent presentation with intuitive visualizations, clear metrics (critical sparsity), and comprehensive appendices supporting reproducibility and ablations
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: top-p framework is straightforward magnitude thresholding applied to modern LLMs without novel algorithms or techniques
No demonstrated practical impact: paper is purely analytical with no acceleration results, speedup validation, or comparison with existing sparsity-based acceleration methods

Shallow theoretical understanding: primarily observational without mechanistic explanations for key findings (e.g., why input sparsity matches gate sparsity, how instruction tuning affects robustness)

Incomplete analysis: massive activations phenomenon acknowledged but dismissed; diffusion LLM analysis is minimal (one model pair); task-dependency is emphasized but not deeply investigated; no layer-wise mechanistic analysis
Overclaimed universality: despite title emphasizing 'universal properties', evidence is more limited given 3 model families, task-dependent variance, and unresolved issues like massive activations

Evaluation limitations: zero-shot likelihood-based evaluation only; reasoning models not directly tested; no validation that data-free methods generalize better than data-calibrated approaches as advocated
Arbitrary design choices insufficiently justified: why 99% accuracy threshold, L1 norm in top-p rule, uniform layer application; robustness to these choices not explored

strengths: Comprehensive and systematic empirical evaluation across multiple model families (Gemma3, LLaMA3, Qwen2.5), sizes (1B-32B), and variants (pretrained, instruction-tuned, reasoning, MoE, diffusion)
First systematic study of activation sparsity in diffusion-based LLMs with novel temporal consistency analysis using Jaccard similarity
Clear and practical framework with the 'critical sparsity' metric that requires no auxiliary training or calibration
Challenges prior assumptions by showing input-based methods match or exceed gate-based approaches, with practical implications for LLM acceleration
Excellent reproducibility with public models/datasets, code to be published, and extensive supplementary analyses including per-task and layer-wise results
Thorough ablation studies on sparsification rules (top-p vs. top-k vs. max-p) demonstrating universality of the approach
Well-written with clear presentation, effective visualizations, and comprehensive coverage of relevant findings
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: the top-p sparsification rule is straightforward and no new algorithms or techniques are proposed; this is fundamentally a characterization paper rather than a methods contribution
Task-dependent sparsity (Figure 4) substantially undermines 'universal properties' claims—critical sparsity ranges from ~20-80% across tasks, contradicting universality narrative

Insufficient theoretical insight into underlying mechanisms: why does sparsity scale with model size? Why do gates have comparable effective ranks yet lower sparsification capacity? Why do input-based methods work well?

Incomplete diffusion-based LLM analysis: despite novelty, Jaccard similarity results show sparsity patterns don't transfer across diffusion steps except early layers, suggesting model-specific solutions are necessary and limiting practical utility
Limited practical impact acknowledged by authors: speedups only 1.3-1.5× versus 4× for alternatives like speculative decoding, and task-dependent patterns complicate deployment
Massive activations phenomenon relegated to appendix despite potential significance for threshold-based approaches; left as 'future work' despite relevance to practical methods
Preliminary MoE analysis with only two models tested; interesting finding about task-variance averaging across experts underdeveloped without clear guidance for practical exploitation
Missing statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, error bars, or multiple runs; 99% performance threshold for critical sparsity lacks sensitivity analysis
Effective rank analysis incomplete: paper acknowledges that effective rank alone insufficient to explain sparsification robustness but provides no further investigation

Limited scope: excludes attention layers, no sub-1B model analysis, restricted to recent model families, zero-shot evaluation only; analysis of layer-specific optimization versus uniform sparsification missing

strengths: Comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple model families (Gemma, LLaMA, Qwen), scales (1B-32B), and variants (pretrained, instruction-tuned, reasoning models)
Clear, general methodology using top-p sparsification applicable without architectural changes or retraining
First systematic analysis of activation sparsity in diffusion-based LLMs
Well-structured presentation with clear figures and detailed appendices supporting reproducibility
Practical finding that input-based sparsification matches/exceeds gate-based approaches, contradicting some prior work
Consistent demonstration that activation sparsity potential increases with model size, with implications for future LLM design
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: Activation sparsity in LLMs is well-established; top-p is a straightforward heuristic; critical sparsity is simply a 1% performance drop threshold
Weak practical impact explicitly acknowledged by authors: effective speedups of only 1.3–1.5× vs. 4× from speculative decoding, undermining efficiency motivation
No actual speedup measurements provided; paper only characterizes which activations are sparse, not whether exploiting sparsity is cost-effective
Task-dependent sparsity (Figure 4) directly contradicts the premise of held-out calibration and undermines practical applicability; paper advocates data-free methods but offers no solution
Core findings are relatively unsurprising: larger models are sparser, different tasks have different requirements, intermediate activations most sparse
Arbitrary design choice of 1% performance drop for critical sparsity without sensitivity analysis; results would substantially differ with alternative thresholds
Instruction-tuning effect on sparsity (Figure 5a) is interesting but completely unexplained and underdeveloped
Incomplete effective rank analysis: finding that gate activations have similar effective rank to intermediates but lower sparsification capacity contradicts main analysis and remains unresolved
Statistical rigor absent: no confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing; appears to use single runs per configuration

Diffusion LLM analysis limited: Jaccard similarity shows sparsity patterns are NOT stable across diffusion steps, limiting practical utility; conclusion that diffusion needs model-specific solutions is vague
Limited experimental coverage: zero-shot evaluation only; no analysis of context length, in-context learning, few-shot, or prompting style effects on sparsity
Missing practical guidance: unclear what practitioners should do differently or when 1.3–1.5× speedup justifies added complexity versus other acceleration techniques
MoE results underdeveloped: per-expert variance analyzed superficially; only 1-2 MoE models tested; generalizability unclear
Missing actionable solutions to task-dependence problem that paper itself identifies as critical limitation

strengths: Comprehensive and systematic study filling a real gap in understanding activation sparsity in modern GLU-based LLMs across multiple model families, scales, and training recipes

Novel empirical insights including: sparsity scaling with model size, input-based sparsity competitiveness with gate-based methods (challenging prior assumptions), and first analysis of activation sparsity in diffusion LLMs
Practical framework: simple top-p sparsification method (training-free, no calibration) and interpretable critical sparsity metric grounded in realistic performance constraints

Rigorous experimental methodology: 9+ evaluation tasks, multiple FFN components, effective rank analysis, temporal pattern analysis for diffusion models, thorough ablations on sparsification methods (top-p vs top-k vs max-p)

Careful experimental treatment including per-task analysis explicitly demonstrating task-dependence, separate analysis of pretrained/instruction-tuned/reasoning models, and per-expert variance analysis in MoE models
Strong reproducibility: code released, open-source models/datasets, clear methodology descriptions, extensive appendices with detailed results

Clear practical implications with evidence of real-world adoption (Gemma3n release mentioned), actionable guidance for practitioners (prefer input sparsity at current scales, use data-free methods to avoid overfitting)
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty—primarily an empirical characterization study; top-p sparsification is straightforward L1-norm-based magnitude thresholding rather than a new technique
Lack of theoretical insight into why sparsity increases with model size; effective rank analysis is suggestive but doesn't explain the causal mechanism, limiting deeper understanding

Task-dependent variance in critical sparsity (Figure 4 shows 20-80% range) contradicts 'universal properties' framing in title/abstract and undermines practical utility of the critical sparsity metric

Disconnection from actual computational benefits—paper characterizes sparsity tolerance but doesn't demonstrate real speedups with the proposed top-p method; relies indirectly on prior work for speedup validation without confirming their specific method achieves predicted gains
Diffusion LLM analysis is preliminary with only one model tested (LLaDA-8B); finding that sparsity patterns don't transfer between diffusion and autoregressive models is important but underexplored

Experimental design choices: 1% performance drop threshold is somewhat arbitrary (no sensitivity analysis), zero-shot evaluation only (unclear if findings generalize to few-shot/fine-tuning), no ablation on batch size effects

Incomplete explanation for why input sparsity matches or exceeds gate sparsity despite gates having comparable effective rank; missing analysis of architectural/training properties driving this surprising finding
Scope limited to FFN layers only (justified but increasingly questioned as context lengths grow); some presentation redundancy in main paper and appendices
